section_summary: This section covers diplomatic communications and political developments regarding Emperor Hirohito of Japan between April 1930 and August 1935. It documents annual presidential birthday greetings and an inaugural trans-Pacific radio broadcast exchange in 1931, followed by reports on assassination attempts including the 1932 Sakuradamon incident and the Hongkew Park bombing, alongside anti-Japanese press reactions in China. It also details the Japanese political controversy surrounding Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's 'Emperor organ theory' and diplomatic representations by the Japanese Embassy over satirical depictions of Hirohito in the American magazine Vanity Fair.

subfiles.about: President Herbert Hoover sends birthday greetings to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: President Hoover sends Emperor Hirohito birthday greetings and wishes for health, happiness and national prosperity.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Hoover to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito thanks President Hoover for his birthday greetings.
subfiles.from: Hirohito, Emperor of Japan
subfiles.summary: Emperor Hirohito telegraphs his heartfelt thanks to President Hoover for the cordial greetings and good wishes received on his birthday.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Hoover
subfiles.to: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Stimson transmits the text of his scheduled radio broadcast address celebrating the Emperor's birthday.
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: The Department of State instructs the Embassy in Tokyo to provide Foreign Minister Shidehara with the text of Secretary Stimson's forthcoming radio address. Stimson reflects on mutual cooperation at the London Naval Conference, highlights the American reception of Prince and Princess Takamatsu, and extends formal felicitations to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Secretary Stimson to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording that the President's telegraphic greeting was superseded by the Secretary of State's radio broadcast.
subfiles.from: Office of Coordination and Review, Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Office of Coordination and Review notes for the file that the telegraphic message from President Hoover to the Emperor was not sent because the Secretary of State transmitted the President's greetings directly via radio broadcast.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Files Regarding President's Greetings

subfiles.about: Nakayama of the Japanese Broadcast Corporation thanks Secretary Stimson for his clear broadcast.
subfiles.from: Nakayama, Japanese Broadcast Corporation
subfiles.summary: Nakayama conveys hearty thanks from Tokyo, confirming that Secretary Stimson's radio broadcast was clearly heard throughout Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Japanese Broadcast Corporation to Secretary Stimson
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Memorandum explaining that opening of US-Japan radio communication conveyed birthday felicitations, rendering a telegram unnecessary.
subfiles.from: Division of International Conferences and Protocol
subfiles.summary: Memo: the new US-Japan radio link was used to convey the President's birthday greetings, replacing the planned telegram.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Transmission of Birthday Felicitations by Radio

subfiles.about: Cancelled draft telegram from President Hoover to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: Cancelled, unsent draft telegram congratulating Hirohito on his birthday and wishing a long, prosperous reign.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Forbes despatch enclosing radio speeches on the Emperor's birthday.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Ambassador Forbes's despatch forwarding clippings of radio speeches on the Emperor's birthday.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Radio Speeches Despatch

subfiles.about: Ambassador Forbes transmits clipping describing the reciprocal American and Japanese radio broadcasts.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Forbes transmits an article from the Japan Advertiser detailing the trans-Pacific radio broadcast exchange on the Emperor's birthday. The broadcast featured introductory remarks, a speech by Secretary Stimson, an address by Foreign Minister Shidehara praising historical ties and disarmament, and musical performances.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 570 from Ambassador Forbes with Press Clipping
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Ambassador Forbes reports a bomb attack on the imperial procession and Cabinet deliberation on resignation.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Forbes reports a young Korean bombed the imperial carriage procession, injuring no one; he signed the palace book as the Cabinet considered resigning.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2 from Ambassador Forbes on Assassination Attempt
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Ambassador Forbes reports in detail on the Sakuradamon bomb incident and the Cabinet's decision to remain in office.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Forbes provides comprehensive analysis of the assassination attempt by Korean laborer Li Ho-sho near Sakurada-mon. He details Prince Saionji's advice against formalistic Cabinet resignation, General Araki's opposition to stepping down, the reaction among younger army officers, and divided press opinion across major Tokyo dailies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 460 on Attempt Against the Emperor and Cabinet Action
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Consul Franklin reports an anti-Emperor article published in Amoy by the Korean Independence Society.
subfiles.from: Lynn W. Franklin, U.S. Consul at Amoy
subfiles.summary: Consul Franklin translates an Amoy article: a Korean Independence Society manifesto on the bomb plot denounces imperial rule, calls the Emperor a military puppet, and warns of more attempts.
subfiles.title: Despatch on Article Attacking Japanese Emperor in Amoy Press
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, U.S. Minister to China

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a Canton Gazette editorial characterizing the Emperor as a military puppet.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, U.S. Consul General at Canton
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Canton Despatch No. 106: a Canton Gazette editorial called the Emperor a puppet of the militarists after the Tokyo bombing.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Canton Gazette Editorial

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting an offensive article regarding the Emperor published in Swatow's Shan Pao.
subfiles.from: David C. Berger, U.S. Consul at Swatow
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Swatow consular report on a Shan Pao article commenting derogatorily on the Korean attempt on the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Shan Pao Article

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and despatch excerpt on offensive article in Tsingtao Min Kuo Jih Pao and its settlement.
subfiles.from: Lewis Clark, U.S. Vice Consul at Tsingtao
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet and excerpt from Tsingtao Despatch No. 709 reporting on local political tensions, tax office seizures by Han Fu-chu, and the settlement of the January 12 incident in which a Japanese mob attacked Tangpu headquarters following the publication of an article insulting the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Despatch Excerpt on Tsingtao Press Incident

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and despatch excerpt regarding Japanese protests over an offensive headline in Shanghai's Min Kuo Jih Pao.
subfiles.from: Edwin S. Cunningham, U.S. Consul General at Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference note and despatch excerpt describing representations by the Japanese Consul General to Mayor Wu Te-chen over a Min Kuo Jih Pao sub-heading expressing regret that only an accompanying carriage was bombed in Tokyo, resulting in official reprimands and disciplinary action against editors.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Despatch Excerpt on Shanghai Min Kuo Jih Pao Incident

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a telegram on the Hongkew Park bombing during the Emperor's birthday celebration.
subfiles.from: Nelson Trusler Johnson, U.S. Minister to China
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Minister Johnson's telegram on the Hongkew Park bombing, which wounded Shigemitsu and General Shirakawa.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Hongkew Park Bombing

subfiles.about: Minister Johnson reports the bombing attack at Hongkew Park during the Emperor's birthday review in Shanghai.
subfiles.from: Nelson Trusler Johnson, U.S. Minister to China
subfiles.summary: Johnson reports a bomb thrown at the speakers' stand during the Emperor's birthday review in Hongkew Park, severely wounding Shigemitsu and Shirakawa.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Minister Johnson on Shanghai Birthday Review Bombing
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: President Hoover extends cordial birthday greetings to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: President Hoover sends cordial birthday greetings and best wishes for continued happiness and well-being to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Hoover to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito reciprocates birthday greetings to President Hoover.
subfiles.from: Hirohito, Emperor of Japan
subfiles.summary: Emperor Hirohito warmly thanks President Hoover for his birthday message and conveys reciprocal good wishes.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Hoover
subfiles.to: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States

subfiles.about: Department instruction quoting the text of President Hoover's birthday message to the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 302 gives the Chargé in Tokyo the text of Hoover's birthday telegram to Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 302 to American Chargé d'Affaires, Tokyo
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a telegram linking the Shanghai bombing to the January Tokyo plot.
subfiles.from: Edwin S. Cunningham, U.S. Consul General at Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Shanghai Telegram No. 237: a Japanese consular officer links the Hongkew Park bombing to the January Tokyo attempt.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Connection Between Tokyo and Shanghai Bombings

subfiles.about: Consul General Cunningham reports inquiries regarding arrested Koreans and Japanese statements linking bombings.
subfiles.from: Edwin S. Cunningham, U.S. Consul General at Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Cunningham reports receiving telegrams from the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom and Philip Ahn concerning the arrest and treatment of Ahn Chang-ho. He confirms Ahn is in good health and reports confidentially that Japanese authorities consider the Shanghai and Tokyo bombings identical in execution and planning.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 237 from Consul General Cunningham
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt conveys congratulations to Emperor Hirohito on his birthday.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: President Roosevelt sends warm congratulations and best wishes for health and happiness to Emperor Hirohito on his birthday.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Department instruction transmitting the text of President Roosevelt's birthday telegram to the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 268 gives the Ambassador the wording of Roosevelt's birthday message to Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 268 to American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt sends cordial birthday felicitations to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: President Roosevelt extends cordial felicitations to Emperor Hirohito on the anniversary of his birth.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito expresses sincere thanks for President Roosevelt's birthday message.
subfiles.from: Hirohito, Emperor of Japan
subfiles.summary: Emperor Hirohito transmits a telegraphic reply thanking President Roosevelt most sincerely for his congratulatory birthday message.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Roosevelt
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States

subfiles.about: Department instruction transmitting the text of President Roosevelt's birthday greetings.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 512 quotes Roosevelt's birthday telegram to Hirohito for the Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 512 to American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between Eugene Dooman and Japanese diplomat Tsuchiya regarding a Vanity Fair article.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Eugene Dooman records his discussion with Tsuchiya of the Japanese Embassy concerning a Vanity Fair article mentioning Emperor Hirohito. Dooman explained that the Department found nothing insolent or malicious in the text and could not request the publisher to suppress such commentary, with which Tsuchiya agreed.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation Regarding Vanity Fair Article

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum on responding to Japanese Embassy complaints about Vanity Fair.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck recommends telling Japanese embassy officials that State finds the Vanity Fair statements non-derogatory and no ground for formal complaint.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Japanese Complaints Against Vanity Fair

subfiles.about: Memorandum and magazine clipping regarding Japanese Embassy representations over a Vanity Fair feature on world monarchs.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Eugene Dooman details a discussion with Second Secretary Ito, who complained that the July 1934 issue of Vanity Fair published photographs and lighthearted descriptions of world monarchs, including Hirohito, that Japan considered insolent. A copy of the illustrated feature is appended.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Mr. Ito on Vanity Fair Publication

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 1208 on Dr. Minobe's constitutional controversy.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviews Ambassador Grew's report on Dr. Minobe's 'Emperor organ theory.' The analysis emphasizes that the dispute reflects an ongoing struggle between militarist reaction and constitutional liberalism, with the military determined to maintain direct imperial access and unrestrained prerogative.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1208 (Minobe Controversy)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports extensively on political and constitutional controversy surrounding Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's organ theory.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew submits an in-depth analysis of the Diet debate provoked by Baron Kikuchi's attack on Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's theory that the Emperor functions as an organ of state. Grew explains Minobe's legal defense, the linguistic and cultural sensitivities regarding imperial sovereignty, and the military's strategic defense of its independent access to the throne.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1208 on Dr. Minobe's Heresy on the Emperor's Position

subfiles.about: Department instruction quoting President Roosevelt's birthday telegram to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 751 gives the Ambassador the text of Roosevelt's congratulatory birthday message to Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 751 to American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt sends birthday congratulations and assurances of high regard to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States
subfiles.summary: President Roosevelt extends congratulations on behalf of the American people and himself to Emperor Hirohito on his birthday anniversary.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito thanks President Roosevelt and the American people for birthday congratulations.
subfiles.from: Hirohito, Emperor of Japan
subfiles.summary: Emperor Hirohito cables his warmest thanks to President Roosevelt and through him to the American people for the birthday congratulations, referred by White House Secretary Louis McH. Howe to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Roosevelt
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Despatch No. 1301 on the government suppression of Dr. Minobe's books.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: The Division summarizes developments in the Minobe controversy, noting that the Home Office banned three of Minobe's books and ordered two others revised, cementing the victory of the absolutist military viewpoint in Japanese politics.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1301

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on the suppression of Dr. Minobe's writings and the dropping of criminal prosecution.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that while Tokyo prosecutors dropped lèse-majesté charges against Dr. Minobe due to lack of disrespectful intent, the Cabinet approved Home Office orders banning three of his books and ordering revisions of two others. Minobe resigned his university lectureships, while Yukio Ozaki stood out as the sole prominent public figure questioning military interference in academic theory.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1301 on Government Action Against Dr. Minobe's Theory

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and despatch excerpt on the latest developments and book bannings in the Minobe case.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference note and excerpt from Tokyo Despatch No. 1304 detailing the dropping of judicial charges against Minobe, official Home Office and Education Ministry directives against subversive ideas, and Minobe's resignations from academic posts.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Excerpt on Dr. Minobe's Constitutional Theory

subfiles.about: Department notifies Embassy Tokyo that the Vanity Fair caricature is not considered offensive and suggests making no comment.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Department finds the Vanity Fair caricature not offensive and tells the Embassy to decline press comment pending Saito's meeting with Hull.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 121 to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull informs Embassy Tokyo of his meeting with Ambassador Saito and press statement denying any official apology.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Hull reports meeting Saito on the Vanity Fair caricature and quotes his press release noting the publisher's disclaimer; reports of a US apology are false.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 123 to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Department repeats Secretary Hull's statement on the Vanity Fair caricature to the Legation in Peiping.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: State sends Peiping Hull's statement on Saito's Vanity Fair representations, to be repeated to Nanking and Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 234 to American Legation, Peiping

subfiles.about: Chargé Neville reports Japanese press agitation and Foreign Office reluctance to escalate the Vanity Fair dispute.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Neville reports that while Japanese headlines inaccurately claimed Secretary Hull expressed regret, the controversy is subsiding. Furthermore, the Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs informally indicated that the Foreign Office had not wanted to make a major diplomatic issue of the caricature.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 164 from Chargé Neville, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull records his comprehensive discussion with Ambassador Saito concerning the Vanity Fair caricature and freedom of the press.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Hull tells Saito and Yoshihara the US guarantees free speech and press, noting publisher Crowninshield disclaimed any offense, while Saito stressed Japanese reverence for the Emperor and sought regret.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation Between Secretary Hull and Ambassador Saito
